description:
Reads one page and reports the technical SEO facts a maintenance retainer is judged on:
title and meta description, heading structure, canonical, Open Graph, hreflang, language,
viewport, images with no alt text, the state of robots.txt and the sitemap, and which
internal links are broken. The sitemap is checked against the rules of the sitemaps
protocol, so a file that exists but that consumers drop is reported as broken rather
than as present.

Use it to answer "why is this page not being indexed?", "does this page have the metadata
it needs?" or "are there broken links on the homepage?". It is the check to run before a
quarterly report, and after a site rebuild.

Do not use it to check whether a site is up, which is uptime_check, or to inspect a
certificate, which is ssl_check. It audits one page: it does not crawl a site, and it
judges only what is in the HTML, never how a page ranks.

robots.txt is read first and obeyed. A page this crawler is not allowed to read is
reported as such and is not requested — and neither are internal links it forbids. An
unreadable robots.txt is treated as forbidding everything, per RFC 9309. A site that gives
no answer at all (the domain does not resolve, its certificate is refused, the connection
fails) is an error, as in uptime_check, not a finding.

Link checking is one HTTP request per link, paced politely, so an audit with links takes
seconds rather than milliseconds; pass checkLinks: false when speed matters more.
Returns findings ordered by urgency, worst first.

checkLinks.description: Whether to request each internal link to find broken ones. Defaults to true. Set it to false for a fast metadata-only audit: link checking is one request per link and is what makes this tool take seconds rather than milliseconds.

maxLinks.description: How many internal links to check at most. Defaults to 25. Links beyond the limit are counted and reported as unchecked, never silently ignored.

url.description: The page to audit, e.g. "https://example.com/pricing". A bare domain such as "example.com" is accepted and read over HTTPS. One page is audited, not a whole site, so pass the page you care about; the homepage is the usual choice. Only http and https URLs are accepted.

name: seo_audit

checkedAt.description: When the audit ran, ISO 8601 in UTC.

fetched.description: Whether the page was read at all. False when robots.txt forbids it.

finalUrl.description: Where it ended up after redirects.

items.description: One actionable observation about the target.

code.description: Stable identifier for this kind of observation, e.g. "cert_expires_soon".

message.description: One sentence explaining the observation in plain words.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

links.description: Internal link health. Only internal links are requested; external ones are counted.

broken.description: Links the site itself says are broken: an HTTP error status (404, 410, 5xx…), a name that does not resolve, or a certificate browsers refuse.

checked.description: How many internal links were actually requested.

couldNotCheck.description: Links that were requested but gave no verdict — a timeout, a dropped connection, a response this client would not read, a 429 — which says nothing about whether they work.

externalTotal.description: Distinct external links found on the page.

internalTotal.description: Distinct internal pages the page links to, ignoring #fragments and links back to itself.

skippedByRobots.description: Internal links this crawler is not allowed to request, so it did not.

unchecked.description: Internal links left unrequested because of the limit.

alternates.description: hreflang alternates declared by the page.

canonical.description: The canonical URL, resolved to absolute.

h1Count.description: How many <h1> elements the page has.

hasViewport.description: Whether a viewport meta tag is present.

imagesMissingAlt.description: Images with no alt attribute at all. An image written alt="" is deliberately decorative and is not listed here.

imagesTotal.description: How many images the page has.

metaRobots.description: The meta robots directive, lowercased, e.g. "noindex, nofollow".

openGraph.description: Open Graph properties, keyed without the "og:" prefix.

robots.description: What the host publishes about crawling, and what it means for this audit.

allowsThisPage.description: Whether the rules permit requesting this URL.

availability.description: "absent" means the host publishes no rules, so everything may be crawled. "unreachable" means the file could not be read, which RFC 9309 says to treat as disallowing everything — so nothing is requested.

crawlDelaySeconds.description: Any Crawl-delay the host asked for, in seconds.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

sitemap.description: The sitemap declared in robots.txt, or /sitemap.xml when none is declared.

checked.description: False when the sitemap could not be requested at all — it timed out, the connection failed, or it was not attempted — so nothing is known about it either way. True whenever the sitemap URL answered, whatever it answered.

compressed.description: Whether it was served gzipped, as a "sitemap.xml.gz". The sitemaps protocol allows this and large sites use it; the file is unpacked before it is read, so every other field here means the same thing either way.

defects.description: Rules of the sitemaps protocol the document breaks, one entry per rule and aggregated by it. Empty when the sitemap is clean, and also when there was nothing readable to check.

code.description: Which rule of the sitemaps protocol is broken, e.g. "namespace", "loc_missing", "lastmod".

count.description: How many entries break this rule. One template mistake breaks it once per URL, so this is the size of the problem, not the number of separate problems.

detail.description: What is wrong and what it costs, in plain words.

example.description: One offending value, for recognition. Null when the rule is about the document itself rather than an entry.

severity.description: warning when a consumer drops the entry or the whole file; info when the value is ignored and the page is still crawled.

entryCount.description: How many <loc> entries it contains — or at least this many, when truncated is true.

found.description: Whether it answered with a usable document.

kind.description: Whether it lists pages or other sitemaps.

missing.description: True only when the sitemap URL answered 404 or 410, meaning there is no sitemap. A site with no sitemap has a gap; a sitemap that is broken, refused (403) or failing (5xx) has a defect, and the findings grade them differently. A sitemap that could not be requested is neither: see checked.

problem.description: Why it is unusable, in plain words.

sampleEntries.description: The first few entries, for recognition.

truncated.description: Whether the sitemap was longer than the read limit and was cut off, in which case entryCount is a floor rather than a total.
Whether the document was longer than the read limit and was cut off.

title: Technical SEO of one page
